lessonTitle: Receptor Tyrosine Kinases and Signal Cascades

blocks.text: A 55-year-old with a melanoma is found to carry a single amino acid change in a kinase called BRAF, and a tablet that blocks that one kinase can shrink the tumour. The change keeps a growth-factor signalling cascade permanently on. To see why, trace the signal from a receptor at the cell surface to the nucleus.

blocks.markdown: **Receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs)** are receptors with an intrinsic enzyme activity: an extracellular ligand-binding domain, a single transmembrane helix and an intracellular **tyrosine kinase** domain. Examples are the receptors for epidermal growth factor (EGFR), insulin and platelet-derived growth factor. A **kinase cascade** is a chain in which each kinase phosphorylates and activates the next.

**The Ras-MAP kinase pathway.** (1) A growth factor such as EGF binds and causes two receptors to **dimerise**. (2) Each receptor's kinase phosphorylates tyrosines on its partner (**trans-autophosphorylation**). (3) These phosphotyrosines are docking sites for proteins with **SH2 domains**; the adaptor **Grb2** binds and brings **SOS**, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor. (4) SOS promotes exchange of GDP for GTP on **Ras**, a small GTPase anchored in the membrane, which becomes active. (5) Ras-GTP activates **Raf** (a MAP kinase kinase kinase), which phosphorylates **MEK** (MAP kinase kinase), which phosphorylates **ERK** (MAP kinase). (6) ERK enters the nucleus and phosphorylates transcription factors, switching on genes that drive cell-cycle entry and proliferation.

rows: Docks on phosphotyrosine and recruits SOS
Active when GTP-bound; intrinsic GTPase turns it off, speeded by GAPs
blocks.caption: Players in the pathway

blocks.title: Tracing a signal
blocks.prompt: EGF binds EGFR on a keratinocyte. List the events until a gene is switched on.

steps.text: Grb2 binds the phosphotyrosines through its SH2 domain and brings SOS, which exchanges GDP for GTP on Ras.
Ras-GTP activates Raf, then MEK, then ERK.
ERK moves into the nucleus and phosphorylates transcription factors, activating genes for proliferation.

blocks.answer: EGFR dimer, Grb2/SOS, Ras-GTP, Raf, MEK, ERK, transcription.

blocks.markdown: **Amplification and termination.** Each active kinase can phosphorylate many substrate molecules, so one receptor event can activate many ERK molecules (a simplified model: if one active Raf phosphorylates 10 MEK and each MEK phosphorylates 10 ERK, one Raf yields about 100 active ERK). Cascades also allow regulation and switch-like responses at several points. The signal is ended by several mechanisms: **protein phosphatases** remove phosphates from receptor and kinases; **GTPase-activating proteins (GAPs)** stimulate Ras to hydrolyse GTP to GDP; and ligand-bound receptors are internalised by endocytosis and degraded in lysosomes. Negative feedback from ERK to upstream components also limits the response.

blocks.title: Constitutive activation drives tumours
blocks.text: A **proto-oncogene** is a normal growth-signalling gene; a gain-of-function mutation or overexpression makes an **oncogene** whose product is active without a ligand. Examples: overexpression or amplification of HER2 (an RTK) in some breast cancers; activating mutations of EGFR in some lung cancers; point mutations in RAS (for example at codon 12) that abolish GTP hydrolysis, leaving Ras locked in the GTP-bound state; the BRAF V600E mutation that makes Raf active without Ras; and BCR-ABL, a fusion tyrosine kinase in chronic myeloid leukaemia. Identifying which component is mutated matters for targeted drugs.

blocks.title: Where is the lesion?
blocks.prompt: A tumour carries a RAS mutation that prevents GTP hydrolysis. Would an EGFR inhibitor stop its ERK signalling? Would a MEK inhibitor?

steps.text: Locked GTP-bound Ras signals downstream of EGFR regardless of receptor activity.
An EGFR inhibitor acts upstream of the lesion, so ERK signalling continues.
A MEK inhibitor acts downstream of Ras, so it can still block the pathway.

blocks.answer: EGFR inhibitor would not help; a MEK inhibitor could.

items: RTK: dimerisation then trans-autophosphorylation on tyrosine; Grb2 (SH2) recruits SOS; SOS activates Ras.
Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK is a serine/threonine kinase cascade ending in transcription.
Termination by phosphatases, Ras GAPs and receptor endocytosis; oncogenic mutations disable control.

blocks.title: Common exam trap
blocks.text: Receptor tyrosine kinases phosphorylate tyrosine residues, whereas the Raf-MEK-ERK kinases phosphorylate serine and threonine. A drug must act downstream of the mutation to be effective.

points: A growth factor dimerises an RTK, which autophosphorylates; Grb2/SOS activate Ras, which drives the Raf-MEK-ERK cascade to the nucleus.
Signals are amplified by each kinase acting on many substrates and are ended by phosphatases, Ras GAPs and receptor internalisation.
Constitutively active RTKs, Ras or Raf drive tumour growth and determine which targeted drugs can work.

questions.stem: Which is the first intracellular event after a growth factor binds a receptor tyrosine kinase?

options.text: Receptor dimerisation followed by trans-autophosphorylation on tyrosines
Hydrolysis of GTP by Ras
Phosphorylation of ERK in the nucleus
Release of calcium from the ER by IP3

questions.correctOptionText: Receptor dimerisation followed by trans-autophosphorylation on tyrosines

distractorRationale.b: Ras hydrolyses GTP to switch off, not at the start.
distractorRationale.c: ERK phosphorylation is a late step.
distractorRationale.d: IP3 belongs to the Gq pathway.

questions.explanation: Ligand binding brings two receptors together so their kinase domains phosphorylate each other's tyrosines. These phosphotyrosines create docking sites for adaptor proteins.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly lists the order of the Ras-MAP kinase cascade after Ras activation?

options.text: Ras, Raf, MEK, ERK
Ras, ERK, MEK, Raf
Raf, Ras, ERK, MEK
MEK, Raf, Ras, ERK

distractorRationale.c: Ras activates Raf, not the reverse.

questions.explanation: Ras-GTP activates Raf (MAPKKK), which phosphorylates MEK (MAPKK), which phosphorylates ERK (MAPK). ERK is the final kinase.

questions.stem: Which protein links phosphorylated receptor tyrosines to Ras activation by promoting GDP-GTP exchange?

options.text: SOS, recruited by the adaptor Grb2
A Ras GAP
A protein phosphatase
Phosphodiesterase

questions.correctOptionText: SOS, recruited by the adaptor Grb2

distractorRationale.b: GAPs stimulate GTP hydrolysis and switch Ras off.

questions.explanation: Grb2 docks on phosphotyrosines and brings SOS to the membrane, where SOS acts as a GEF for Ras. GAPs do the opposite by speeding GTP hydrolysis.

questions.stem: Which mechanism directly terminates the signal from active Ras?

options.text: GTP hydrolysis to GDP, stimulated by a GTPase-activating protein
Binding of a second growth factor
Phosphorylation of Ras by ERK on tyrosine
Increased SOS activity

questions.correctOptionText: GTP hydrolysis to GDP, stimulated by a GTPase-activating protein

distractorRationale.c: ERK is a serine/threonine kinase and does not switch Ras off this way.

questions.explanation: Ras has a weak intrinsic GTPase that GAPs accelerate; the resulting Ras-GDP is inactive. Phosphatases and receptor internalisation act elsewhere in the pathway.

questions.stem: A colon tumour has a RAS mutation that abolishes GTP hydrolysis. Which statement is most likely true?

options.text: Ras stays GTP-bound and drives ERK signalling even if an EGFR inhibitor blocks the receptor
Ras is permanently GDP-bound and the tumour is signalling-deficient
The tumour requires continuous EGF to signal
A MEK inhibitor will have no possible effect

questions.correctOptionText: Ras stays GTP-bound and drives ERK signalling even if an EGFR inhibitor blocks the receptor

distractorRationale.b: Loss of hydrolysis leaves Ras GTP-bound.
distractorRationale.d: MEK is downstream of Ras and can still be inhibited.

questions.explanation: A mutation that stops GTP hydrolysis locks Ras in the active state downstream of the receptor. Drugs acting upstream, like EGFR inhibitors, cannot switch it off.

questions.stem: A melanoma carries the BRAF V600E mutation, which makes Raf kinase active without Ras. Which effect is expected?

options.text: MEK and ERK are continuously phosphorylated, driving proliferation
The cascade is inhibited because Raf is overactive
Receptor dimerisation becomes essential
Only Ras-GTP levels fall

questions.correctOptionText: MEK and ERK are continuously phosphorylated, driving proliferation

distractorRationale.b: An active Raf drives the cascade.
distractorRationale.c: The mutation bypasses the receptor and Ras.

questions.explanation: An active Raf phosphorylates MEK, which phosphorylates ERK, whatever the upstream signal. This constitutive activation is why a specific BRAF inhibitor can be effective.

questions.stem: Outline how a growth factor signal is transmitted from an RTK to the nucleus through the Ras-MAP kinase pathway.
markingGuide: Ligand binding causes receptor dimerisation and trans-autophosphorylation on tyrosines.
Grb2 binds phosphotyrosines via its SH2 domain and recruits SOS.
SOS exchanges GDP for GTP on Ras, activating it.
Ras-GTP activates Raf, which phosphorylates MEK, which phosphorylates ERK.
ERK enters the nucleus and activates transcription factors for proliferation.
questions.explanation: A complete answer follows the sequence of components in order and states the biochemical event at each stage.

questions.stem: Explain how signal amplification and signal termination are achieved in a kinase cascade.
markingGuide: Each activated kinase phosphorylates many molecules of the next kinase, so the signal is amplified step by step.
Cascades allow regulation and switch-like responses at multiple points.
Termination by phosphatases dephosphorylating receptors and kinases.
Ras GAPs stimulate GTP hydrolysis, inactivating Ras.
Receptor endocytosis and degradation, and negative feedback, also limit the response.
questions.explanation: Amplification comes from catalytic activity at each level; termination requires reversing each activation step.

questions.stem: Compare three ways in which constitutive activation of a signalling protein can drive tumour growth: HER2 overexpression, RAS mutation and BRAF V600E.
markingGuide: HER2 overexpression: excess RTK signalling with or without ligand, drives pathways such as Ras-MAPK.
RAS mutation: loss of GTP hydrolysis leaves Ras GTP-bound and active, independent of the receptor.
BRAF V600E: Raf kinase active without Ras, so MEK and ERK are continuously phosphorylated.
Position in the pathway determines whether upstream or downstream inhibitors are effective.
All remove the normal requirement for ligand and the normal off-switch.
questions.explanation: Each lesion removes a brake at a different level, so a drug must act at or below the lesion.

questions.stem: True or false: Ras is activated when SOS promotes exchange of GDP for GTP.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Ras is active in its GTP-bound form, and SOS is the guanine nucleotide exchange factor that loads GTP. Ras then switches itself off by hydrolysing GTP, a process speeded by GAPs.
